body:
Review pass 17. Everything was under a minute old (metric-learning.R at 51s), so rather than report a no-op I built the external reference Epic 6 will need. Pure base R, no package code.

Epic 6 acceptance says "null estimates center at zero and planted effects recover the declared conditional target within a prespecified Monte Carlo error". That needs three things: a target, a tolerance, and proof the test discriminates. Here they are.

Setup: n=120, q=4, p=30, R=6 runs, contrast (1,-1,0,0), spatially correlated Sigma, planted effect on the contrast direction. Estimator is the ordered-pair crossvalidated Mahalanobis form - the same tr[(cc^T) B_a K B_b^T] this epic evaluates with a supplied true precision.

  true squared Mahalanobis target : 3.728339
  NULL    mean = +0.003071   MC se = 0.004899   z = +0.63
  SIGNAL  mean = +3.714054   MC se = 0.020777   bias = -0.014284   z(bias) = -0.69

Unbiased on both arms at 400 replications.

PRESPECIFIED TOLERANCES, 3 x MC se at nrep=400, adopt directly if useful:
  null    |mean| < 0.01470
  signal  |mean - target| < 0.06233
MC se goes as 1/sqrt(nrep) - ~0.0098 at 100 reps, ~0.0031 at 1000. Pick nrep from the tolerance you want, not a round number.

THE IMPORTANT PART - the criterion discriminates. Same simulation, NON-crossvalidated estimator (single-run delta Sigma^-1 delta^T), under the null:

  mean = +1.9725   instead of 0

About 400 MC standard errors away. So this test would immediately catch an implementation that silently stopped cross-validating. That matters because a recovery test which passes for both the correct and the broken estimator proves nothing - my original review flagged that the suite had no parameter-recovery tests at all, and this is the shape the first one should take.

Suggest asserting both arms: null centering is the sensitive one, signal recovery is what rules out an estimator that is unbiased under the null but wrongly scaled under signal.

Reproducible with set.seed(2026). Note is on Epic 6.
